transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I can plan everything out in detail, but when it’s time to actually sit down and do the work, I just can’t seem to make myself stick with it for more than a few minutes. It has been making it really hard to get my career started after graduating, and I'm just feeling really stuck.
Did these concentration and follow-through problems start in childhood or early school years, or did they begin only recently as you’ve been feeling stuck?

While the severe stagnation with my applications has been going on for the last two years, these issues actually date back to childhood. Even in elementary school, I would constantly forget my worksheets, leave projects to the last minute, and get report card comments like "bright but careless" because I'd skip parts of assignments.
Did you also have ongoing problems with being easily distracted, losing things, or fidgeting/restlessness as a child, or was it mainly trouble finishing tasks and being careless?

It was definitely more about trouble finishing tasks, being careless, and forgetting things, rather than any physical restlessness or fidgeting. I would constantly forget to bring home the right worksheets and lose track of long-term projects until the night before. That's why I got those "bright but careless" comments on my report cards, because I'd skip parts of assignments or miss easy questions.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, like at work or school and also at home or in conversations?

Yes, they definitely happen in multiple settings. It really impacted my schoolwork during my final semesters of college, and now at home, my struggle to finish application packets is causing a lot of tension with my parents. I also notice it in conversations, where I'll ramble on about niche art history topics to friends and family without realizing they've lost interest.
Do you often make careless mistakes, have trouble sustaining attention on reading or paperwork, or seem to not listen when someone is speaking to you?

I definitely make a lot of careless mistakes, like leaving whole questions blank on applications or making embarrassing typos despite trying to be careful. My attention span is also a major hurdle—I'll get easily distracted googling random things or feel completely mentally exhausted after just a few minutes of trying to focus. I don't think "not listening" is really an issue for me, though.
Before age 12, did you also often feel restless, interrupt others, act without thinking, or have trouble waiting your turn, or was it mainly inattention and forgetfulness?

It was definitely just the inattention and forgetfulness; I don't recall ever being restless, interrupting others, or having trouble waiting my turn. Instead, I was the kid who constantly forgot worksheets, left projects to the last minute, and got report card comments like "bright but careless" because I'd skip parts of assignments.
Do these attention and organization problems still cause significant problems in your daily life now, such as at work, school, or managing responsibilities at home?

Yes, they are causing major problems right now. Because I keep stalling on applications and missing deadlines, I'm currently unemployed, living back at home, and feeling like my life is completely on hold. This has created a lot of tension with my parents, who are frustrated and think I'm just not following through, even though I have the qualifications to move forward.
Before age 12, did you have these attention and organization problems continuously, or were there long periods when they were not present?

Yes, it was definitely a continuous, ongoing pattern for me back in elementary school rather than something that came and went. I consistently struggled with forgetting worksheets, losing track of long-term projects until the last minute, and getting "bright but careless" comments on my report cards for skipping parts of assignments.

Do these attention and organization problems also happen in everyday tasks like paying bills, keeping appointments, or managing chores, and have they caused problems in more than one area of your life for at least six months?

Yes, they absolutely affect my daily life; despite calendar reminders, I still constantly forget to follow up on emails or even show up to my psychiatrist appointments on time. This has been a continuous issue for about two years now, stalling my career transition, leaving me unemployed, and causing a lot of tension at home with my parents.
Have you ever had significant problems with hyperactivity or impulsivity, such as feeling unable to sit still, interrupting others, blurting things out, or acting without thinking?

No, I’ve never really struggled with physical restlessness, interrupting others, or acting impulsively. However, I do sometimes talk excessively, rambling on and on about museum politics or obscure artists to my friends and family. I usually only realize I'm doing it when I notice their eyes glaze over or they try to change the subject.
Do these attention and organization problems cause similar difficulties in at least two settings, such as work/school and home, and have they been present for more than 6 months?

Yes, they absolutely do, and it has been a constant struggle for about two years now since my final semesters of college. Professionally, it has stalled my career and graduate school applications, while at home, it causes constant tension with my parents because I'm still living here and struggling with daily follow-through.
Did you have these attention and organization problems before age 12 in a clear, ongoing way, or did they first appear later in adolescence or adulthood?

Yes, they definitely started back in elementary school, well before I was 12. I was always the kid who forgot to bring home worksheets, left projects until the last minute, and got report card comments like "bright but careless" because I'd skip parts of assignments.
Do you currently have any symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity, such as feeling unable to sit still, fidgeting, interrupting others, blurting things out, or acting without thinking?

I don't experience physical hyperactivity, fidgeting, or acting impulsively without thinking. However, I do struggle with talking excessively, specifically rambling on about art history or museum politics to my friends and family. I usually don't realize I'm doing it until I notice their eyes glaze over.
Do you often lose things you need for daily tasks, like keys, phone, paperwork, or school/work materials, or get distracted by unrelated thoughts or noises when trying to focus?

Losing physical items like my keys or phone isn't really an issue for me, but getting distracted by unrelated thoughts is a major, constant problem. When I'm trying to focus on an application, I'll suddenly find myself googling train schedules, rearranging my bookshelf, or getting lost in thoughts about a movie I saw. Before I even realize it, twenty minutes have gone by and I've barely written a single sentence.
Do you often feel internally restless, like you need to keep moving or you have trouble relaxing even if you are not physically fidgeting?

No, I don't really feel internally restless or have a need to keep moving. My struggle is much more about mental blocks, procrastination, and having a really hard time focusing on my work. It feels more like I'm mentally stuck rather than physically unable to relax.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a lifelong, childhood-onset pattern of inattention and disorganization with impairment in multiple settings, persisting into adulthood and causing significant functional decline. The patient confirms distractibility, careless mistakes, failure to finish tasks, procrastination, forgetfulness, and difficulty sustaining attention, with onset before age 12 and ongoing impairment for years. Hyperactivity/impulsivity is largely absent, but ICD-10 F90.0 is the best match among the provided candidates.
